newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa air force returns to flood-hit Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa air force returns to flood-hit Mozambique.

text.p: The South African Air Force (SAAF) said on Monday it was sending its aircraft back into flood-hit Mozambique, just three days after ending a four-day operation to evacuate flood victims.

SAAF spokeswoman Laverne Machine said in a statement that Mozambique had asked for the planes to return to help in airlifting vital supplies to the Tete and Caia regions of the resource-rich but poor southern African country.
About 30 tonnes of medical supplies, blankets food and clothes will be distributed by the SAAF and helicopters from the Zimbabwean Air Force.
Last week the SAAF evacuated 1,411 people and airdropped 4,500 kg (10,000 lb) of supplies to people along the flooding Pungue, Buzi and Zambezi rivers.
The Mozambique government has appealed for international aid to help relocate an estimated 400,000 people affected by the floods.
